anatomy.flutter: IconSwap(icons: List<Widget>, activeIndex, window, cell) builds a fixed-size SizedBox + ClipRect + Stack where every icon occupies the same cell (`alignment: Alignment.center`, one Stack) and is offset `(i - strip position) * step` via Transform.translate, with the active cell additionally wrapped in `_squashed` for the jelly scale.
anatomy.web: IconSwap({active, icons: Record<string, ReactNode>, className}) renders a `<span className="relative inline-grid place-items-center overflow-hidden">` with each icon in a `col-start-1 row-start-1` span (all sharing one CSS grid cell) offset via `--swap-offset` CSS var read by the `swap-roll` utility, with the active cell's inner span carrying `anim-change`.

api.flutter: IconSwap requires `window` (the clip box, e.g. 20 or 24px) and `cell` (the strip cell's own glyph height, e.g. 16 or 20) as EXPLICIT required parameters, documented as: 'DIVERGENCE. The browser measures this; here it is declared... it is not clamped or corrected, because there is nothing to correct it against.'
api.web: IconSwap takes only `active`, `icons`, and `className` — no width/height/cell props at all; the window size comes entirely from whatever sizing class (e.g. `size-5`, `size-6`) is passed via `className`, and the per-step travel distance is resolved by the browser measuring each icon span's own rendered box.
api.note: Reclassified on review from `gap`: the shortfall recorded below is on the FLUTTER side — the web has the capability, or Flutter's own doc comment records it as not ported, or Flutter reproduces an earlier state of the web source that has since moved on. This ledger measures the web's convergence onto Flutter's vocabulary, so it is a pass here. The worker's original finding is kept verbatim after this line, because the finding is still true and still worth a Flutter reader's attention. ORIGINAL: Not a rendering defect (both sides are documented as intentionally equivalent when the caller supplies matching numbers), but it is a real API-surface gap: a Flutter caller must manually keep `window`/`cell` in sync with whatever glyph size is actually rendered, with zero runtime correction if they drift, whereas the web version measures the DOM automatically and can never desync. A design-system consumer copying an IconSwap call from the web doc to Flutter has no `window`/`cell` values to read off the web API since those props do not exist there — they must be derived by hand from the Icon `size` prop used inside. File/line: lib/src/components/ui/icon_swap.dart:96-118; components/ui/icon-swap.tsx:20-30 (no window/cell props).

states.flutter: _from/_to track roll position in steps; `didUpdateWidget` captures `_from = _strip(_rollT)` (current mid-flight position) before re-aiming, so 'A transition interrupted mid-flight restarts from the value on screen, not from the target it was abandoning.' `_squash.forward(from: 0)` replays on every index change, and once more on first mount via `didChangeDependencies`.
states.web: Each active span remounts via `key={isActive ? 'landed-${activeIdx}' : 'waiting'}` so 'Remounts on arrival so the squash replays every time'; the roll itself is a CSS transition on `--swap-offset` via `transform`, which by definition restarts smoothly from its current computed value when the target changes mid-flight (CSS transitions always interpolate from current computed style).

disabled.flutter: IconSwap has no `enabled`/disabled concept in icon_swap.dart — it is purely decorative and 'Put it inside a Button as the child, never beside one,' so disabled state belongs entirely to the containing Button.
disabled.web: icon-swap.tsx defines no disabled styling; the component has no notion of being disabled independent of whatever Button wraps it.
disabled.note: IconSwap is decorative content inside a Button on both platforms, not an independently disable-able control — disabled state and its visual treatment belong to the Button, documented on that component's own page.

interaction.flutter: icon_swap.dart mounts no GestureDetector/FocusNode of its own — activeIndex is driven entirely by the parent rebuilding the widget with a new value; IconSwap itself has zero pointer/keyboard handling.
interaction.web: icon-swap.tsx attaches no onClick/tabIndex — it is a pure presentational span whose `active` prop is controlled entirely by the parent.
interaction.note: IconSwap is a controlled, non-interactive display primitive on both platforms — all pointer/keyboard interaction belongs to the Button (or other control) that changes its `active`/`activeIndex` prop, not to IconSwap itself.

semantics.flutter: Every non-active cell is wrapped `ExcludeSemantics(excluding: i != _to, ...)`, and the class doc states plainly: 'the reference marks every inactive cell aria-hidden and puts the accessible name on the Button that contains the IconSwap ... so the port excludes the inactive cells from the semantics tree and contributes no name of its own.'
semantics.web: Each icon span carries `aria-hidden={!isActive}`, hiding every non-active cell from the accessibility tree while leaving the active one exposed; the component itself sets no aria-label, matching the Flutter doc's 'contributes no name of its own' contract.
